body.working_title: What MuseScore users ask for: unmet needs around arranging and parts

body.text: Which unmet needs do MuseScore users raise most often in the MuseScore project's public feature requests, and where do needs about arranging, parts and instrumentation rank among them?

body.text: Exploration set (RN4, RN5): most-reacted requests concern platform packaging (Flatpak, Muse Hub on Linux), notation details and playback. Reactions are sparse (RS7: 500 in total; RS8: median 0). No request in the exploration set asks for automatic arranging or reduction to a given ensemble; the nearest are smarter staff merge/split (implode/explode: #16897, #25347), an instrumentation sheet (#24421), and flagging unplayable or hard notes and chords (#25499, #21609, #21559). The keyword theme rules are noisy: some matches are incidental words in issue bodies.

body.text: Forum scan (musescore.org), qualitative, no counts: users periodically ask MuseScore to arrange or re-voice music for a given set of instruments: a piano score into a woodwind quintet (2014, https://musescore.org/comment/96875), an 'Arrange for' command from scanned piano music (2014, https://musescore.org/en/node/42911), automatic orchestration of piano chords (https://musescore.org/en/node/291410), parts for alternative transposing instruments (2017, https://musescore.org/en/node/259001). Replies consistently say there is no automatic method; the workarounds are Explode/Implode, manual copy-paste, and the Arrange Parts plug-in, which supports only MuseScore 1.x and does not fit notes to instrument ranges (https://musescore.org/project/arrange-parts).

Context, qualitative: Muse Hub's arrangements page (https://www.musehub.com/arrangements) promotes ready-made arrangements from a score library that users can open and edit in MuseScore Studio; it mentions no service for commissioning custom arrangements. Freelance marketplaces list paid services for arranging sheet music for any set of instruments (Upwork, Fiverr; page contents not retrieved).

Limitation: Reddit threads could not be read from this environment, and forum pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, so the forum scan supports statements about kinds of requests, not their frequency.

body.rationale: Rule of PL3: s = 0.0459 < threshold 0.10 on the held-out set (RN6).
Rule of PL2: notation and engraving had 215 reactions; input, workflow and UI had 250 (and playback 185), so n <= ui.

body.text: Both deciding runs carry the flag 'holdout used elsewhere': the held-out file was written by the split run RN3 (which reported only counts) and was then used by both RN6 and RN7. RN7 repeats RN6's computation under the second plan; one plan per hypothesis was used because a plan carries a single decision rule. Classifier limitation: keyword rules match incidental words in issue bodies, so theme counts measure keyword-defined themes, not hand-coded topics.
